To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the initiation of crack tip extension in a solid rocket propellant is affected by the presence of a circular hole or steel inclusion.

the strain energy density factor (S.E.D.) at the crack tip is a function of the crack tip position relative to the hole or the circular inclusion and that the S.E.D. is also a function of the normal distance of hole or circular inclusion from the crack axis.

the initiation of crack propagation in the presence of a circular hole or an inclusion can occur at a distance from the hole or inclusion center which is less than that in the absence of the hole or inclusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the initiation of fracture in a solid propellent containing a circular hole or an inclusion.
a nonlinear finite deformation analysis of a solid propellants containing a circular hole or circular inclusion and subjected to a uniform tensile displacement.
the development of a numerical model for predicting the initiation of crack propagation in an orthotropic solid propellant containing a crack and a hole or an inclusion.

the initiation of crack propagation is strongly influenced by the distance of the hole and the inclusion from the crack tip and the normal distance from the crack axis of the center of the hole and/or the inclusion.

, in general, the presence of a hole or a circular inclusion has a detrimental effect on the initiation of crack propagation, but the effect depends on the relative position of the hole or inclusion with respect to the crack axis.

, in general, the presence of a hole or inclusion reduces the crack tip stress intensity factor and, therefore, reduces the probability of crack extension in the solid propellant.
